The National Weather Service's active alerts feed for Arizona, checked directly today, lists no Excessive Heat Warning, Watch, or Advisory anywhere in the state; the only active statewide alert is a Flood Warning for the Gila River below Painted Rock Dam in Yuma and Maricopa Counties, effective through November 17, which does not affect this trail (Source: National Weather Service). Hike before 7am or after 6pm and carry extra water.

tanque-verde-ridge.note: Saguaro National Park's conditions page, checked today, continues to indicate the east (Rincon Mountain) district's trails are open, with a standing caution that hikers should use extra care in areas burned by two 2020 fires where ground may be unstable and trees may fall, and that Happy Valley Road has stream crossings worth checking on with the visitor center first (Source: National Park Service). Call the Rincon Mountain Visitor Center at 520-733-5153 for specifics on current trail conditions. The National Weather Service's active alerts feed for Arizona, checked directly today, lists no Excessive Heat Warning, Watch, or Advisory anywhere in the state; the only active statewide alert is a Flood Warning for the Gila River below Painted Rock Dam in Yuma and Maricopa Counties, effective through November 17, which does not affect this trail (Source: National Weather Service). Hike before 7am or after 6pm and carry extra water.

south-kaibab-ooh-aah.note: Grand Canyon National Park's Key Hiking Messages confirm South Kaibab Trail remains open from the South Kaibab Trailhead to Black Bridge, which covers Ooh Aah Point and Cedar Ridge well within the open section; a reopening of this segment below the Tipoff and the connecting River Trail was reported in late October 2026 (Source: National Park Service, Grand Canyon National Park). Black Bridge and Silver Bridge, which span the Colorado River, remain closed due to hazardous conditions from flash flooding, so through-hikes to Phantom Ranch or the North Rim are not possible, with no estimated reopening at this time. Potable water is available at the South Kaibab Trailhead tank only. Call the Backcountry Information Center at 928-638-7875 to confirm current status before descending.

bright-angel-indian-garden.note: Grand Canyon National Park's Key Hiking Messages confirm Bright Angel Trail remains open from the Bright Angel Trailhead to the River Resthouse, which covers Havasupai Gardens (formerly Indian Garden) well within the open section (Source: National Park Service, Grand Canyon National Park). The park expects delays of about 30 to 45 minutes just above the Three Mile Resthouse for rockfall mitigation work starting November 18, 2026, three days from today; as of today's check this work has not yet started. Water is off at the Three Mile and Mile and a Half Resthouses and at Havasupai Gardens to conserve water. Stock use is also closed between Mile-and-a-Half Resthouse and Havasupai Gardens. Beyond River Resthouse, Black Bridge and Silver Bridge remain closed with no estimated reopening, so Phantom Ranch and the river crossing stay inaccessible. Confirm current status with the Backcountry Information Center at 928-638-7875 before descending.

rim-trail.note: Grand Canyon National Park's Key Hiking Messages list no new trail closures beyond the North Rim's seasonal and construction closures, which do not affect the South Rim's Rim Trail, and do not name the Rim Trail among any inner canyon corridor trail closures (Black Bridge, Silver Bridge, and the entirety of North Kaibab Trail) (Source: National Park Service, Grand Canyon National Park). Use caution near the rim during any lightning.

north-kaibab-coconino.note: The entirety of North Kaibab Trail, from the North Kaibab Trailhead to Phantom Ranch, including Cottonwood Campground, remains closed following significant flash flooding in Bright Angel Canyon on August 29, 2026. Grand Canyon National Park's Key Hiking Messages reconfirm the North Kaibab Trail, Black Bridge, Silver Bridge, and the entire Phantom Ranch facility, including the canteen, Bright Angel Campground, and all overnight lodging, remain closed with no estimated reopening at this time (Source: National Park Service, Grand Canyon National Park). A separate waterline project closure between Redwall Bridge and the north end of Cottonwood Campground, which started October 15, 2026, keeps a hard closure on this trail in place through approximately February 2027; outside reporting in late October 2026 corroborated this timeline. Bright Angel and Cottonwood Campgrounds remain closed indefinitely.
